strategies.name: htf_fvg_tap_with_1m_ifvg_reversal

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: we always going to be trading from 9:30 till 11:30 a.m. New York time
entry_sequence.action: Only look for setups after 9:30 a.m. New York time within the 9:30-11:30 a.m. session.
entry_sequence.rationale: The speaker wants the setup traded during the active NY morning volume window.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: identify your draw on liquidity. So, the very first step is identify your draw on liquidity
entry_sequence.action: Identify the draw on liquidity first: for shorts, if a buy-side level like Asia high, London high, previous day high, or equal highs is taken, look to the opposite-side liquidity below; for longs, if a sell-side level like Asia low, London low, previous day low, or equal lows is taken, look to the opposite-side liquidity above.
entry_sequence.rationale: The draw on liquidity defines where price is expected to move next.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: after 9:30, you're waiting for price to create a 5m minute fair value gap towards your draw on liquidity
entry_sequence.action: After 9:30, wait for a 5-minute fair value gap to form toward the draw on liquidity; if no 5-minute gap forms, use a 15-minute fair value gap instead.
entry_sequence.rationale: The higher-timeframe fair value gap is the IRL zone used for the setup.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: wait for price to tap into the higher time frame IRL which is your 5m minute fair value gap
entry_sequence.action: Wait for price to tap into that higher-timeframe fair value gap, then drop to the 1-minute chart.
entry_sequence.rationale: The entry is only considered once price returns into the higher-timeframe IRL.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: make sure on the one minute price has swept some of liquidity before tapping into the 5minut fair value gap
entry_sequence.action: On the 1-minute chart, require a liquidity sweep before the inversion trigger: for shorts, sweep a 1-minute high before the tap; for longs, sweep a 1-minute low before the tap.
entry_sequence.rationale: The speaker wants a sweep of nearby 1-minute liquidity before entry confirmation.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: you simply wait for price to close below this one minute fair value gap
entry_sequence.action: For shorts, enter when price closes below the 1-minute bullish fair value gap, inverting it into resistance. For longs, enter when price closes above the 1-minute bearish fair value gap, inverting it into support.
entry_sequence.rationale: The 1-minute inversion is the actual entry trigger.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: if there are three, you're going to wait for all of those three fair value gaps to get inversed
entry_sequence.action: If there are multiple 1-minute fair value gaps in the manipulation leg, wait for all of them to be inversed before entering.
entry_sequence.rationale: The speaker requires full inversion of all relevant 1-minute gaps when more than one appears.

stop.transcript_quote: you want to put your stop above the high
stop.rationale: The speaker says to put the stop above the high for shorts, and the long example mirrors this below the recent low/bodies.

strategies.stop_management: Go break even as soon as the closest liquidity after entry is taken out.

targets.transcript_quote: you can target the drawn liquidity
targets.rationale: The speaker says one target option is the draw on liquidity.

targets.transcript_quote: you can go for 1:2 fixed risk-to-reward ratio
targets.rationale: The speaker says you can go for a fixed 1:2 risk-to-reward ratio.
